summary: Q1 revise-apply resolved all three 129-review-apply Blocking Findings by closing the authority boundary at every production-reachable path. (Q1-RA-001) The raw RunResultFile terminal publisher is no longer exported: writeRunResult and publishTerminalResult are module-private, and completeRun is the only externally reachable terminal-completion API. Callers provide only typed descriptors (consumedRunIds / producedArtifactTags / reviewedRunId / reviewVerdict / reviewFindings); Core derives every ResultRef from actual target bytes. The shared completion preflight is Action-requiredness based: artifact-producing Actions (explore/revise-explore/propose/revise-propose — not review-*) unconditionally require the complete producedResultRefs, and review-apply unconditionally requires the Core-derived verificationSummaryRef; missing evidence keeps the Run pending (no terminal publication). Negative tests prove a raw or incomplete terminal publication is mechanically unavailable. (Q1-RA-003) One shared stage-aware effective-set completeness validator (validateStageEffectiveSet) is now used at terminal preflight, review entry, AND Reader current-generation validation. Initial explore must exactly bind explore.md; initial propose must bind proposal.md + design.md + tasks.md + the complete current specs namespace. readRunProducedResultRefs no longer converts missing/malformed/absent evidence to [] — it throws SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED. Review entry unconditionally validates the reviewed Run's stage effective set (no length > 0 guard), and the Reader produces a FactConflict for empty/partial current-generation produced sets. (Q1-RA-005) Every descriptor is runtime-validated before filesystem resolution: validateRunIdDescriptor reuses the formal parseRunId grammar for reviewedRunId / sourceReviewRun / consumedRunIds; resolveRunResultPath and readReferencedRunResult reject path-shaped values (../x, a/b, C:\tmp\run, result.json); producedArtifactTags are runtime-validated against permittedProducedArtifactTags(action) with unknown/disallowed tags, empty/undefined revise changed-tag sets, and tags on non-artifact Actions rejected at the descriptor boundary. All verification checks actually executed and passed: typecheck, lint, build, 515 tests (515 pass, 0 fail), OpenSpec change strict, 8/8 canonical specs strict, git diff --check. Delivery Full Test was NOT run (no authorization for revise-apply). No contract artifacts, prior Runs, or Flowkit state were modified; no Git commit was created by this Run.

resolvedFindings.evidence: The raw RunResultFile terminal publisher is no longer a production-reachable API: src/persistence/run-persistence.ts no longer exports writeRunResult (it and publishTerminalResult are module-private; export surface is verified by the 'completeRun is the ONLY public terminal-completion entry (RA-001)' import-surface test in tests/unit/persistence/run-persistence.test.ts). All terminal completion enters through completeRun(runDir, CompleteRunInput), which accepts typed descriptors only — no ResultRef-valued fields. Core derives every ResultRef via deriveActionResult (buildRunResultRef / buildArtifactResultRef / deriveReviewVerdictRef / deriveVerificationSummaryArtifactRef). The shared completion preflight is Action-requiredness based: artifact-producing Actions unconditionally require producedResultRefs and validateStageEffectiveSet; review-apply unconditionally requires the Core-derived verificationSummaryRef; any missing evidence throws and leaves the Run pending (assertMutable + fs.link create-once preserved in the single private publisher). Negative tests prove raw caller-authored terminal completion is rejected and that completeRun requires the complete initial produced set and the review-apply verification summary.

One shared stage-aware effective-set completeness validator, validateStageEffectiveSet (src/persistence/result-ref-adapter.ts), is used at all three sites: completion preflight (run-persistence.ts completionPreflight), review entry (run-persistence.ts validateReviewEntry, called unconditionally — the producedRefs.length > 0 guard is removed and requiredness comes from artifactStage(reviewedFact.action)), and Reader current-generation validation (formal-fact-reader.ts validateCurrentGenerationRefs). Initial explore exactly binds explore.md (count 1, identity, kind produced-artifact, fingerprint = current bytes); initial propose exactly binds proposal.md + design.md + tasks.md + the complete current canonical specs/** namespace. Missing, malformed, empty, or partial produced sets fail closed regardless of field presence: readRunProducedResultRefs throws SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED on missing/unreadable/invalid-JSON/absent-actionResult (never converts to []), review entry rejects before publish (RESULT_REF_MISMATCH), and the Reader emits artifact-effective-set-incomplete FactConflicts (unit-tested for empty and partial propose produced sets). The empty-specs-namespace-does-not-excuse-missing-singletons edge is explicitly covered by a review-entry negative test.

Every descriptor is runtime-validated before filesystem resolution. validateRunIdDescriptor (src/persistence/result-ref-adapter.ts) reuses the formal parseRunId grammar (src/domain/run-id.ts) and is applied to reviewedRunId and sourceReviewRun in validateContextFile (src/persistence/serialization.ts), to consumedRunIds and reviewedRunId/sourceReviewRun in validateCompleteRunInput (run-persistence.ts), and inside resolveRunResultPath / readReferencedRunResult so path-shaped values (../x, a/b, C:\tmp\run, result.json, arbitrary filenames) are rejected with RUN_ID_INVALID_FORMAT before any path.join. producedArtifactTags are runtime-validated in validateCompleteRunInput against permittedProducedArtifactTags(action): unknown tags reject, Action-disallowed tags reject (revise-explore with proposal, apply with proposal), revise-propose with empty or undefined changed-tag sets reject (no no-op inheritance), revise-explore requires exactly ['explore']. Negative tests cover all of the above, including the raw descriptor boundary (no TypeScript-only reliance).
